The snippet is a virtual file at examples/spending-alerts/__b121_entry_validation__.ts. It imports the real library union `NodeVersion` from the package alias `@graphrefly/ts/core`, which re-exports it from packages/ts/src/node/versioning.ts (packages/ts/src/core/index.ts lines 31-40). No fabricated input type is introduced: the parameter is exactly `readonly (NodeVersion | undefined)[]`.

Discrimination uses the library's own `level` field, not a replacement tag. `NodeVersionV0` is `{ readonly level: 0; readonly counter: number }` and `NodeVersionV1` is `{ readonly level: 1; readonly counter: number; readonly cid: string; readonly prev: string | null }`, with `NodeVersion = NodeVersionV0 | NodeVersionV1` (versioning.ts lines 27-39). `undefined` is the disabled case because `createNodeVersion` returns `undefined` when the resolved policy is not enabled (versioning.ts lines 113-117). The function maps inputs in order and copies `counter`, `cid` and `prev` verbatim, so counter 0 and prev null are preserved; it performs no hashing, comparison or identifier creation.

On the three questions:

1. Is `cid` a source-code revision? No. It is a content identifier computed from the node's DATA value, not from source code. `computeV1Cid` hashes `strictCanonicalJsonBytes(value)` (versioning.ts lines 74-79), and `advanceNodeVersion` recomputes it from the new value (lines 137-143). It identifies the versioned data content, not a code revision.

2. Does equal `cid` prove equal implementation or I/O authorization? No. The cid is a hash of canonical data bytes only (versioning.ts lines 74-79); it carries no information about the function/implementation that produced the value, and no authority or permission facts. Equal cid therefore cannot prove equal implementation, and it says nothing about I/O authorization. Authorization is a separate concern (the README distinguishes permission grants in the localAuthority input group, examples/spending-alerts/README.md lines 75-80).

3. Does an unchanged content identifier necessarily imply an unchanged counter? No. The counter is advanced independently of the cid: `advanceNodeVersion` increments `counter` by one on every advance (versioning.ts lines 134-143), while the cid is recomputed from the value. If a node advances with a value whose canonical bytes hash to the same cid (e.g. the same data re-advanced), the counter still increases while the cid stays the same. Conversely, a changed cid does not by itself tell you the counter delta. So an unchanged cid does not imply an unchanged counter.
